accepted-gaps.description: Whether the resolved plan carries an accepted policy gap in this area. Required, so a caller that forgets it fails at parse rather than silently publishing nothing.

area.description: Package area, as `sniff repo package-area` names it (e.g. claudine, claudine/rendezvous, root).

measure-compiler-work.description: Count actual rustc invocations around each measured test command. Baseline collection only; defaults off so an ordinary run is byte-identical to the uninstrumented one.

rows.description: This area's dispatch row document, produced by `affected_scope.row_sets`: `{test, check, lint, wsl}` — four disjoint sets that together partition the area's executing cells — plus the scalar `has_*_rows` flags this workflow guards on. A row is `{package, gate, environment, runner}` and nothing else.

slug.description: The area name spelled for artifact names (`/` -> `--`). Presentation only; `--area` still receives the real name.

tested-revision.description: The resolved plan's `head`: the one revision this whole run tests, and the only checkout `ci-build` will produce or verify an archive against. Required, and never recomputed here — see the `env:` comment in `ci.yml`.

lint-rows.description: JSON array of this area's `lint` rows. Each row is `{package, gate, environment, runner}`.

set -euo pipefail

detail=""
if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then

  --arg package "$PACKAGE" --arg job "$JOB" --arg environment "$ENVIRONMENT" \
  --arg result "$result" --arg detail "$detail" --argjson dependents "${DEPENDENTS:-[]}" \
  '{package: $package, job: $job, environment: $environment, result: $result, dependents: $dependents}

python3 - "${{ matrix.package }}" <<'PY'

import subprocess
import sys
import time

started = time.monotonic()

set -euo pipefail
just _ci_build_report \
  "${{ steps.counter.outputs.wrapper }}" \
  "${{ steps.counter.outputs.counter_dir }}" \
  "$RUNNER_TEMP/measurement/measurement.json" \

cd darkmatter && just zed-verify

set -euo pipefail
python3 scripts/ci/companion_suites.py \
  --suites "$COMPANION_SUITES" \
  --environment "$ENVIRONMENT" \
  --gate lint \
  --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/companions.json"

set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/status"
# `result` is the CELL's conclusion, not the job's (see the header).
#
# INVARIANT, companions-only cell: its required work IS its companion
# suites, so the companion step's outcome is the cell's outcome and
# ONLY `success` passes. Clippy was `if`-gated off above, so its
# `skipped` outcome carries no information — reading it as a failure
# would block every pull request that touches a Rust file, and
# reading it as a pass would let a cell that ran NOTHING go green,
# which is the false full-tree evidence this cell exists to prevent.
# The ordinary branch is untouched: there `skipped` still means "not
# this cell's work" and only an explicit `failure` downgrades.
companion_uncovered=""
result="$JOB_STATUS"
if [ "$COMPANIONS_ONLY" = "true" ]; then
  if [ "$result" = "success" ] && [ "$COMPANION" != "success" ]; then
    result=failure
    companion_uncovered=1
    echo "::error title=${PACKAGE} ${JOB} (${ENVIRONMENT}) failed::companion lint: ${COMPANION}. This cell runs no clippy of its own, so a companion that did not succeed leaves it with no evidence."
  fi
elif [ "$result" = "success" ] && { [ "$GATE" = "failure" ] || [ "$ZED" = "failure" ] || [ "$COMPANION" = "failure" ]; }; then
  result=failure
  echo "::error title=${PACKAGE} ${JOB} (${ENVIRONMENT}) failed::clippy: ${GATE}; Zed extension: ${ZED}; companion lint: ${COMPANION}."
fi
companions='{}'
if [ -f "$COMPANIONS_FILE" ]; then
  companions="$(cat "$COMPANIONS_FILE")"
fi
detail=""
if [ "$COMPANION" = "failure" ] || [ -n "$companion_uncovered" ]; then
  failed="$(jq -r '[to_entries[] | select(.value.outcome != "success") | .key] | join(", ")' <<<"$companions")"
  if [ -n "$companion_uncovered" ]; then
    detail="companion suite(s) ${failed:-unreported} lint produced no success evidence; this cell lints nothing of its own, so nothing else covers them"
  else
    detail="companion suite(s) ${failed:-unreported} lint FAILED; clippy's result does not cover them"
  fi
fi
# An unmeasured duration is ABSENT: the lint step never ran (a
# cancelled job, or a companions-only cell that skips clippy on
# purpose) and inventing a measurement for it would be a fabrication
# (AC13). Nothing downstream divides by it — the empty string is
# dropped from the document here rather than coerced to a number. A
# RECORDED duration is emitted exactly as the step measured it,
# fraction included — `0.4` is a fast clippy run, and only the absent
# field means "not recorded".
jq -nc \
  --arg package "$PACKAGE" \
  --arg job "$JOB" \
  --arg environment "$ENVIRONMENT" \
  --arg result "$result" \
  --arg detail "$detail" \
  --arg duration "$GATE_DURATION" \
  --argjson companions "$companions" \
  '{package: $package, job: $job, environment: $environment, result: $result}
   + (if $detail == "" then {} else {detail: $detail} end)
   + (if $duration == "" then {} else {duration_s: ($duration | tonumber)} end)
   + (if ($companions | length) == 0 then {} else {companions: $companions} end)' \
  >"$RUNNER_TEMP/status/status.json"

set -euo pipefail
python3 scripts/ci/completion.py \
  --plan ci-artifacts/ci-resolved-plan/resolved-plan.json \
  --cell '${{ steps.cell.outputs.cell }}' \
  --artifacts ci-artifacts \
  --companions "$RUNNER_TEMP/companions.json" \
  --target '${{ steps.cell.outputs.target }}' \
  --run "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
  --attempt "$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT" \
  --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/completion/completion.json"

  --head '${{ inputs.tested-revision }}' \

# A backend that cannot exist here skips silently inside require_level!.
# Naming every declared backend and its status turns "0 run / N skipped"
# from an invisible non-event into a readable row. Which ones this cell
# must prove is the plan's decision (the cell's `backends`), not a
# name test here.
{
  echo "### L2 backends — ${PACKAGE} on ${ENVIRONMENT}"
  echo ""
  echo "| backend | status |"
  echo "|---|---|"
  while IFS= read -r backend; do
    [ -n "$backend" ] || continue
    if [ "$(jq -r --arg b "$backend" 'index($b) != null' <<<"$REQUIRED_BACKENDS")" = "true" ]; then
      echo "| ${backend} | required by the plan — its tests MUST execute |"
    elif [ "$backend" = "apple-terminal" ] && [ "$ENVIRONMENT" = "macos-latest" ]; then
      echo "| apple-terminal | unavailable — \`available()\` returns false when CI is truthy; its tests skip |"
    else
      echo "| ${backend} | unavailable — needs a live GUI session; its tests skip |"
    fi
  done < <(printf '%s' "$DECLARED_BACKENDS" | jq -r '.[]?')

echo "$sidecars" >>"$GITHUB_PATH"
if [ -x "$sidecars/stub_dunstify" ] || [ -x "$sidecars/stub_dunstify.exe" ]; then

    echo "BISCUIT_BACKEND_PROOF_BIN=$proof" >>"$GITHUB_ENV"

set -euo pipefail
# The plan's declared suites and required backends, in the spelling
# the recipe records them as provenance. `completion.py` refuses a
# disagreement between these and the plan rather than preferring one,
# so the list is the cell's verbatim — never narrowed here.
suites="$(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"${BISCUIT_CI_COMPANION_SUITES:-[]}")"
export BISCUIT_CI_COMPANION_SUITES="$suites"
if [ "$GATE" = "L2" ]; then
  required="$(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"${REQUIRED_BACKENDS:-[]}")"
  if [ -n "$required" ]; then
    export BISCUIT_TEST_REQUIRED_BACKENDS="$required"
  fi
fi
archive_args=()
if [ -n "${ARCHIVE_FILE:-}" ]; then
  archive_args=(--archive-file "$ARCHIVE_FILE" --workspace-remap "$ARCHIVE_WORKSPACE")

  export BISCUIT_JUNIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT="$ARCHIVE_WORKSPACE"
  export BISCUIT_JUNIT_TARGET_DIR="$ARCHIVE_WORKSPACE/target"
fi
just _expected_manifest "$GATE" "${{ matrix.package }}" \
  ${archive_args[@]+"${archive_args[@]}"} ${{ steps.cell.outputs.test_args }}

set -euo pipefail
just _ci_build_counter "${{ matrix.gate }} ${{ matrix.environment }}"

set -euo pipefail
tier_args=()
case "$GATE" in
  L1)
    # --no-fail-fast: run ALL of the package's tests so one slow or
    # failing test cannot suppress the rest of the suite's evidence.
    tier_args=(--no-fail-fast)
    ;;
  L2)
    # --no-fail-fast, for the same reason as L1: a truncated report
    # costs a full round-trip to learn what the second failure was,
    # and L2 is the tier whose backends the author's host may not
    # have. The shared-pane suites are safe to run on: the broker's
    # pane is torn down by `_test_l2`'s trap rather than by a test,
    # and both profiles set `retries = 0`.
    tier_args=(--no-fail-fast)
    # Execution proof, not just availability: require exactly the
    # backends the plan attached to this cell — the subset of the
    # package's declaration its environment hosts, the same list the
    # expected manifest recorded and `completion.py` will demand a
    # proof for. With BISCUIT_TEST_REQUIRED_BACKENDS set, `_test_l2`'s
    # backend-proof bracket fails the tier when a required backend
    # produced zero executed tests and writes `backend-proofs.json`
    # into the staging tree — an installed tmux plus a suite that
    # skipped everywhere must not render a green cell.
    required="$(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"${REQUIRED_BACKENDS:-[]}")"
    if [ -n "$required" ]; then
      export BISCUIT_TEST_REQUIRED_BACKENDS="$required"
    fi
    # L2 runs in parallel unless the package declared `l2-serial`
    # (with its reason) in `[package.metadata.ci.tests]`.
    if [ "$(jq -r 'contains(["l2-serial"])' <<<"$RUNNER_TOOLS")" = "true" ]; then
      export BISCUIT_L2_THREADS="${BISCUIT_L2_THREADS:-1}"
    else
      export BISCUIT_L2_THREADS="${BISCUIT_L2_THREADS:-$(just _test_l2_threads)}"
    fi
    ;;
esac
# Archive mode passes the verified archive and remaps the workspace to
# this checkout; the declared feature flags are already baked in and
# `_archive_drop_build_flags` removes them. Nothing here is a Cargo
# build flag, so this invocation cannot reach a compiler.
archive_args=()
if [ -n "${ARCHIVE_FILE:-}" ]; then
  archive_args=(--archive-file "$ARCHIVE_FILE" --workspace-remap "$ARCHIVE_WORKSPACE")
  # The knobs that keep the recipe off Cargo entirely: nextest as a
  # standalone binary, and the workspace and target directory the
  # JUnit staging would otherwise ask `cargo metadata` for. A
  # consumer's `cargo metadata` would succeed on a hosted runner and
  # fail in the toolchain-free guest — one spelling for both. The
  # planner's key helper is the same kind of unintended build: the
  # verified `ci-build` is already here, so a planner test must not
  # `cargo run` a cold one.
  export BISCUIT_NEXTEST_BIN='cargo-nextest nextest'
  export BISCUIT_JUNIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT="$ARCHIVE_WORKSPACE"
  export BISCUIT_JUNIT_TARGET_DIR="$ARCHIVE_WORKSPACE/target"
  export INSTA_WORKSPACE_ROOT="$ARCHIVE_WORKSPACE"
  : "${ARCHIVE_KEY_HELPER:?verification did not report the ci-build key helper}"
  export BISCUIT_CI_BUILD_BIN="$ARCHIVE_KEY_HELPER"
fi
started="$(date +%s)"
status=0
just "$RECIPE" "${{ matrix.package }}" \
  ${tier_args[@]+"${tier_args[@]}"} \
  ${archive_args[@]+"${archive_args[@]}"} ${{ steps.cell.outputs.test_args }} || status=$?
# The gate's own duration, recorded whether it passed or failed. In
# the pre-cutover schedule this window contains BOTH the compile and
# the test run — they are one Nextest invocation — which is why the
# compiler-work count, not this number, is the compile evidence.
echo "seconds=$(( $(date +%s) - started ))" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [ -n "${JOB_STARTED_EPOCH:-}" ]; then
  echo "setup_seconds=$(( started - JOB_STARTED_EPOCH ))" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi
exit "$status"

just _ci_build_report \
  "${{ steps.counter.outputs.wrapper }}" \
  "${{ steps.counter.outputs.counter_dir }}" \
  "$RUNNER_TEMP/measurement/measurement.json" \
  "${{ matrix.package }}" "${{ matrix.environment }}" "${{ matrix.gate }}"

set -euo pipefail
python3 scripts/ci/companion_suites.py \
  --suites "$COMPANION_SUITES" \
  --environment "$ENVIRONMENT" \
  --gate "$GATE" \
  --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/companions.json"

set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/status"
# An unmeasured stage is absent, never zero: a job that reported no
# timings at all must not read as one whose transfer was instant. A
# malformed measurement is treated the same way — this step runs under
# `always()` and is the cell's only evidence, so instrumentation must
# not be able to lose it.
timings="${TIMINGS:-}"
if ! printf '%s' "$timings" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timings='{}'
fi
# `result` is the CELL's conclusion, not the job's (see the header).
result="$JOB_STATUS"
if [ "$result" = "success" ] && { [ "$GATE" = "failure" ] || [ "$COMPANION" = "failure" ]; }; then
  result=failure
  echo "::error title=${PACKAGE} ${JOB} (${ENVIRONMENT}) failed::${JOB} tests: ${GATE}; companion suites: ${COMPANION}."
fi
# Every DECLARED companion suite records its own outcome, counts, and
# command duration, not only on failure: a SKIPPED companion leaves no
# other evidence, and the rollup downgrades a green Rust cell whose
# declared companion produced no success evidence (R12).
companions='{}'
if [ -f "$COMPANIONS_FILE" ]; then
  companions="$(cat "$COMPANIONS_FILE")"
fi
detail=""
if [ "$COMPANION" = "failure" ]; then
  failed="$(jq -r '[to_entries[] | select(.value.outcome != "success") | .key] | join(", ")' <<<"$companions")"
  detail="companion suite(s) ${failed:-unreported} FAILED; the Rust JUnit report does not cover them"
fi
# The build this cell executed, when it executed one. Reporting only;
# the cell's identity stays `{package, environment, gate}` and the
# rollup keys nothing on a build.
jq -nc \
  --arg package "$PACKAGE" \
  --arg job "$JOB" \
  --arg environment "$ENVIRONMENT" \
  --arg result "$result" \
  --arg detail "$detail" \
  --arg key "${BUILD_KEY:-}" \
  --arg producer "${BUILD_PRODUCER:-}" \
  --arg digest "${BUILD_DIGEST:-}" \
  --argjson companions "$companions" \
  --argjson timings "$timings" \
  '{package: $package, job: $job, environment: $environment, result: $result}
   + (if $detail == "" then {} else {detail: $detail} end)
   + (if ($companions | length) == 0 then {} else {companions: $companions} end)
   + (if $key == "" then {}
      else {build: {key: $key, producer: $producer, digest: $digest}} end)
   + (if $timings == {} then {} else {timings: $timings} end)' \
  >"$RUNNER_TEMP/status/status.json"

set -euo pipefail
python3 scripts/ci/completion.py \
  --plan ci-artifacts/ci-resolved-plan/resolved-plan.json \
  --cell '${{ steps.cell.outputs.cell }}' \
  --expected-manifest "target/nextest/ci-reports/expected-${{ matrix.gate }}.json" \
  --artifacts target/nextest/ci-reports \
  --companions "$RUNNER_TEMP/companions.json" \
  --backend-proofs target/nextest/ci-reports/backend-proofs.json \
  --target '${{ steps.cell.outputs.target }}' \
  --run "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
  --attempt "$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT" \
  --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/completion/completion.json"

set -euo pipefail
python3 scripts/ci/hosted_observations.py emit \
  --plan ci-artifacts/ci-resolved-plan/resolved-plan.json \
  --cell "$CELL" \
  --stage target/nextest/ci-reports \
  --completion "$RUNNER_TEMP/completion/completion.json" \
  --gate-outcome "$GATE_OUTCOME" \
  --run-id "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
  --attempt "$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT" \
  --workflow "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF" \
  --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/observation/observation.json"

row.description: ONE dispatch row, `{package, gate, environment, runner}`, as the planner derived it for this area. Everything else this leg needs — the package's test arguments, its slow-test contract, its runner tools, its native prerequisites, and the build record it consumes — is resolved from the run's `ci-resolved-plan` artifact by `scripts/ci/cell_contract.py`, which refuses a row the plan does not schedule before the guest is even provisioned.

tested-revision.description: The resolved plan's `head`: the one revision this whole run tests, and the only checkout `ci-build` will verify an archive against. The guest clone below inherits it from the runner checkout. Required, and never recomputed here — see the `env:` comment in `ci.yml`.

steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
python3 scripts/ci/cell_contract.py \
  --plan ci-resolved-plan/resolved-plan.json \
  --row "$ROW" \
  --head '${{ inputs.tested-revision }}' \
  --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

python3 scripts/ci/build_status.py \
  --status ci-build-status/build-status.json \
  --package '${{ steps.cell.outputs.package }}' \
  --key '${{ steps.cell.outputs.build_key }}' \
  --producer '${{ steps.cell.outputs.build_producer }}' \
  --artifact '${{ steps.cell.outputs.build_artifact }}'
echo "epoch=$(date +%s)" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
sleep 90

set -euo pipefail
uname -a
# WSL2 runs a real Linux kernel and says so; WSL1's syscall translation
# layer reports a Microsoft build instead. A silent downgrade to WSL1
# would make every WSLg-dependent package (playa, messenger,
# biscuit-clipboard, biscuit-visualized, renderable) report its
# no-capability fallback, and NAT'd networking would stop applying to
# sniff, homelab, and rendezvous.
case "$(uname -r)" in
  *microsoft-standard-WSL2*) ;;
  *)
    echo "guest is not WSL2 (kernel: $(uname -r)); refusing to report a result" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

set -euo pipefail
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if apt-get update && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends \
      ca-certificates curl git xz-utils jq python3; then
    jq --version
    python3 --version
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "apt attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 30s" >&2
  sleep 30
done
echo "guest package installation failed three times" >&2
exit 1

set -euo pipefail
id -u biscuit >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -s /bin/bash biscuit
# Passwordless sudo so recipes that self-elevate (apt installs in
# `_ensure-native-libs`) keep working if ever invoked as the user.
echo 'biscuit ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' >/etc/sudoers.d/biscuit
chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/biscuit

set -euo pipefail
# `wsl-bash` starts in the translated workspace directory, so `pwd` is
# the one workspace path that needs no WSLENV forwarding to be correct.
workspace="$(pwd)"
git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
revision="$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse HEAD)"

guest_root='${{ env.GUEST_ROOT }}'
rm -rf "$guest_root" '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}'
# `git clone` creates the leaf but not the intervening directories, and
# the guest has no such path until something makes it.
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$guest_root")" '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}'
# Building over the workspace pays the 9p boundary penalty on every
# file access; ext4 is both faster and where real WSL developers keep
# their repositories, so it is the configuration worth testing.
git clone --no-hardlinks "$workspace" "$guest_root"
git -C "$guest_root" checkout --detach "$revision"

cp -R "$workspace/ci-build-artifact/." '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/'
cp "$workspace/ci-resolved-plan/resolved-plan.json" '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/'
# The test step runs as `biscuit` (see the user-creation step); every
# tree it touches must be writable by that user, not root.
chown -R biscuit:biscuit "$guest_root" '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}' /home/biscuit

set -euo pipefail
# Deliberately NOT rustup: the guest only RUNS prebuilt test binaries
# from the archive, so a Rust toolchain would add minutes and buy
# nothing. cargo-nextest executes an archive without Cargo or rustc.
curl_get() {
  curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSfL \
    --retry 5 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors \
    --connect-timeout 15 "$@"
}
# A retried download must target a file: stdout cannot be rewound, so
# streaming a partial response into tar would preserve corrupt bytes.
download_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$download_dir"' EXIT
curl_get --output "$download_dir/just.tar.gz" \
  'https://github.com/casey/just/releases/download/${{ env.JUST_VERSION }}/just-${{ env.JUST_VERSION }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz'
tar xzf "$download_dir/just.tar.gz" -C /usr/local/bin just
curl_get --output "$download_dir/nextest.tar.gz" \
  https://get.nexte.st/latest/linux
tar xzf "$download_dir/nextest.tar.gz" -C /usr/local/bin
just --version
cargo-nextest nextest --version

set -euo pipefail
# A WSL2 guest IS Linux, so it consumes the `ubuntu-latest` package
# list — the same dependency-closure union the producer installed.
# Satisfying only the producer is insufficient when an archived binary
# dynamically links a library the guest lacks.
#
# Interpolated, NOT read from `env:`: step env lives on the Windows
# host process, and `wsl-bash` forwards only WSLENV-listed variables
# into the guest — an `env:`-sourced $NATIVE is unbound here.
cd '${{ env.GUEST_ROOT }}'
native_args=()
while IFS= read -r package; do
  if [ -n "$package" ]; then native_args+=("$package"); fi
done < <(jq -r '.[]?' <<<'${{ steps.cell.outputs.native_packages }}')
if [ ${#native_args[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  just _ensure-native-libs "${native_args[@]}"
fi

set -euo pipefail
# The 9p workspace, before the `cd`: `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` is a Windows
# path this guest cannot write, so every measurement the host needs
# crosses back as a file the status step reads (the same reason the
# manifest is read on the host).
workspace="$(pwd)"
mkdir -p "$workspace/wsl-timing"
cd '${{ env.GUEST_ROOT }}'
export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
started="$(date +%s)"
status=0
just _ci_build_verify \
  '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}' \
  '${{ steps.cell.outputs.build_artifact }}' \
  wsl2-ubuntu \
  '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/resolved-plan.json' || status=$?
echo "$(( $(date +%s) - started ))" >"$workspace/wsl-timing/verify.seconds"
# Written whether or not the build was accepted: a refused cell's
# transfer and verification cost is exactly what a reader wants.
cp '${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/${{ steps.cell.outputs.build_artifact }}.verdict.json' \
  "$workspace/wsl-timing/verdict.json" 2>/dev/null || true
exit "$status"

# Headroom on the volume the guest's VHDX grows into. This number is
# the whole diagnosis: compare it against the extracted size of the
# package's archive.
Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem |
  Select-Object Name, @{n='UsedGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Used/1GB,1)}},
                      @{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Free/1GB,1)}} |
  Format-Table | Out-String | Write-Host

set -uo pipefail
workspace="$(pwd)"
mkdir -p "$workspace/wsl-diag"
{
  echo "=== $(date -u +%FT%TZ) guest census ==="
  uname -a
  echo "--- filesystem backing each path extraction touches ---"
  for path in /tmp / /home; do
    # -T resolves the mount for a PATH, so this is correct whether or
    # not the directory is itself a mount point.
    findmnt -T "$path" -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,SIZE,AVAIL 2>&1 || echo "$path: findmnt failed"
  done
  echo "--- df ---"
  df -h / /tmp /home 2>&1
  echo "--- memory ---"
  free -m
  swapon --show 2>&1 || true
} 2>&1 | tee "$workspace/wsl-diag/guest-census.txt"

set -euo pipefail
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  exec runuser -u biscuit -- env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR HOME=/home/biscuit USER=biscuit LOGNAME=biscuit bash "$0"
fi
guest_root='${{ env.GUEST_ROOT }}'
export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
sidecars='${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/${{ steps.cell.outputs.build_artifact }}-sidecars'
if [ -d "$sidecars" ]; then
  export PATH="$sidecars:$PATH"
fi
export BISCUIT_CI_ENVIRONMENT='${{ env.BISCUIT_CI_ENVIRONMENT }}'
export NEXTEST_PROFILE='${{ env.NEXTEST_PROFILE }}'
export BISCUIT_L1_INCLUDE_SLOW='${{ steps.cell.outputs.l1_include_slow }}'
export BISCUIT_NEXTEST_BIN='cargo-nextest nextest'
export BISCUIT_JUNIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT="$guest_root"
export BISCUIT_JUNIT_TARGET_DIR="$guest_root/target"
export BISCUIT_JUNIT_STAGE_DIR="$guest_root/target/nextest/ci-reports"
archive='${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/${{ steps.manifest.outputs.archive_name }}'
[ -f "$archive" ] || { echo "the verified archive is missing at $archive" >&2; exit 1; }
cd "$guest_root"
just _expected_manifest '${{ steps.cell.outputs.gate }}' \
  '${{ steps.cell.outputs.package }}' \
  --archive-file "$archive" \
  --workspace-remap "$guest_root" \
  ${{ steps.cell.outputs.test_args }}

set -euo pipefail
# Drop to the unprivileged user: root ignores file permissions, which
# inverts permission-denial fixtures (claudine's readonly-file and
# shadow-home-copy tests, sniff's worktree-registry test). `env`
# preserves the wrapper environment while giving the user its own
# HOME, which tests that write under HOME rely on.
# `-u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`: the preserved environment carries root's
# `/run/user/0`, and `just` dies with EACCES trying to use it as the
# unprivileged user — which took out every guest leg on run
# 31415404872. Unset, it falls back to a user-writable location.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  exec runuser -u biscuit -- env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR HOME=/home/biscuit USER=biscuit LOGNAME=biscuit bash "$0"
fi
# Re-exported from the job-level `env:` block through GitHub expression
# interpolation rather than read from the guest environment: whether
# `wsl-bash` forwards a given variable depends on WSLENV, and the
# result identity is far too consequential to leave to that. A missing
# or wrong BISCUIT_CI_ENVIRONMENT does not fail — it silently files
# these results under the native Windows cell.
export BISCUIT_CI_ENVIRONMENT='${{ env.BISCUIT_CI_ENVIRONMENT }}'
export NEXTEST_PROFILE='${{ env.NEXTEST_PROFILE }}'
export COLORTERM='${{ env.COLORTERM }}'
export BISCUIT_L1_INCLUDE_SLOW='${{ steps.cell.outputs.l1_include_slow }}'
guest_root='${{ env.GUEST_ROOT }}'
# WSL appends the Windows host PATH by default. On hosted runners that
# adds dozens of /mnt/c entries, so every intentionally missing binary
# probe crosses the 9p boundary dozens of times. Claudine performs many
# such discovery probes; the inherited PATH turned sub-second tests
# into 20-second tests and made this serial, archive-only lane take
# hours. The guest is intentionally self-contained and installs every
# required executable under the standard Linux prefixes above.
export PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
# Every compile-time tool the package declared reaches the guest as a
# VERIFIED build sidecar. Nothing is built here, and the guest proves
# it has no toolchain to build one with.
sidecars='${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/${{ steps.cell.outputs.build_artifact }}-sidecars'
if [ -d "$sidecars" ]; then
  export PATH="$sidecars:$PATH"
  if [ -x "$sidecars/stub_dunstify" ]; then
    export MESSENGER_STUB_BIN_DIR="$sidecars"
  fi
fi
if command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1 || command -v rustc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "the wsl2-ubuntu cell requires a toolchain-free unprivileged guest" >&2
  exit 1
fi
# No Cargo in the guest, so the canonical recipe must reach nextest as
# a standalone binary and stage its JUnit report without shelling out
# to `cargo metadata`. See fixes/2026-07-27-refactor/wsl-archive-requirements.md.
export BISCUIT_NEXTEST_BIN='cargo-nextest nextest'
export BISCUIT_JUNIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT="$guest_root"
export BISCUIT_JUNIT_TARGET_DIR="$guest_root/target"
# insta finds the workspace root by running `cargo metadata`; with no
# cargo in the guest its manifest-dir fallback DOUBLES the snapshot
# path (darkmatter/lib/darkmatter/lib/...), every .snap looks absent,
# and each snapshot test fails while rendering correct output — 165
# phantom failures on run 30791562395. Pin the root explicitly.
export INSTA_WORKSPACE_ROOT="$guest_root"
export BISCUIT_JUNIT_STAGE_DIR="$guest_root/target/nextest/ci-reports"

archive='${{ env.GUEST_BUILD }}/${{ steps.manifest.outputs.archive_name }}'
[ -f "$archive" ] || { echo "the verified archive is missing at $archive" >&2; exit 1; }

# DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Started HERE rather than in its own step so it is
# unambiguously alive across extraction — a background process from an
# earlier `wsl-bash` invocation would depend on surviving that
# invocation's exit, which is exactly the assumption a dying guest
# breaks. It writes across the 9p mount, ON PURPOSE: a log on ext4 is
# unreachable from the Windows host once the VM is gone, and a VM that
# is gone is the case being diagnosed. Self-limiting so nothing outlives
# the job's own ceiling.
workspace="$(pwd)"
mkdir -p "$workspace/wsl-diag"
cat >/tmp/biscuit-sampler.sh <<'SAMPLER'
#!/bin/bash
out="$1"
for _ in $(seq 1 400); do
  {
    printf '%s' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
    df -BM --output=target,avail /tmp / /home 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -s ' \n' ' '
    printf '| memAvailMiB=%s' "$(awk '/MemAvailable/{print int($2/1024)}' /proc/meminfo)"
    printf ' | %s\n' "$(tr '\n' ' ' </proc/pressure/memory 2>/dev/null)"
  } >>"$out"
  sleep 10
done
SAMPLER
chmod +x /tmp/biscuit-sampler.sh
setsid nohup /tmp/biscuit-sampler.sh \
  "$workspace/wsl-diag/guest-resources.log" >/dev/null 2>&1 &

# --workspace-remap is not optional: the archive records the PRODUCER's
# source paths, and the guest checkout is its own clone. Declared
# feature flags are passed along and dropped by
# `_archive_drop_build_flags` — they were baked into the archive.
cd "$guest_root"
started="$(date +%s)"
status=0
just _test "${{ steps.cell.outputs.package }}" \
  --no-fail-fast \
  --archive-file "$archive" \
  --workspace-remap "$guest_root" \
  ${{ steps.cell.outputs.test_args }} || status=$?
# The gate's own window, recorded whether it passed or failed and
# carried back across the 9p mount for the host's status step. It
# contains the extraction nextest performs inside the run, which is
# why the verifier reports its own extraction separately.
mkdir -p "$workspace/wsl-timing"
echo "$(( $(date +%s) - started ))" >"$workspace/wsl-timing/l1.seconds"
exit "$status"

set -uo pipefail
# The upload runs on the Windows host, which cannot read ext4, so the
# reports cross the 9p mount once, at the end, rather than per test.
workspace="$(pwd)"
rm -rf "$workspace/wsl-junit"
mkdir -p "$workspace/wsl-junit"
# The CONTENTS of the staging root, so `manifest.jsonl` lands at the
# artifact root. `ci-rollup` reads the manifest only from there;
# copying `target/nextest/` instead would bury it one level down.
cp -R '${{ env.GUEST_ROOT }}/target/nextest/ci-reports/.' \
  "$workspace/wsl-junit/" 2>/dev/null || true
# Staging must never change the tier's outcome.
exit 0

set -uo pipefail
workspace="$(pwd)"
mkdir -p "$workspace/wsl-diag"
{
  echo "=== $(date -u +%FT%TZ) guest post-mortem ==="
  df -h / /tmp /home 2>&1
  free -m
  # An OOM kill or an ext4 I/O error — the two ways a backing store
  # failure becomes a signal — are both recorded here and nowhere else.
  echo "--- dmesg tail ---"
  dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -120
} 2>&1 | tee "$workspace/wsl-diag/guest-postmortem.txt"

# The VHDX only ever grows, so a Windows volume that is full HERE was
# full when the guest died. This is the measurement that separates "the
# guest filled its own filesystem" from "the guest's disk could not grow
# because the host had nothing left to give it".
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
# wsl.exe emits UTF-16 by default, which is why it renders as spaced-out
# characters in the raw Actions logs. WSL_UTF8 makes it emit UTF-8
# instead. Reaching for [Console]::OutputEncoding would be the wrong
# lever: it also governs what pwsh WRITES, so it would garble this
# step's own output to fix someone else's.
$env:WSL_UTF8 = '1'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path wsl-diag | Out-Null
$report = @("=== host post-mortem $(Get-Date -Format o) ===")
$report += Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem |
  Select-Object Name, @{n='UsedGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Used/1GB,1)}},
                      @{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Free/1GB,1)}} |
  Out-String
$report += "--- wsl --status ---"
$report += (wsl.exe --status 2>&1 | Out-String)
$report += "--- wsl --list --verbose ---"
$report += (wsl.exe --list --verbose 2>&1 | Out-String)
$report += "--- backing VHDX ---"
# Bounded depth: a recursive sweep of the whole profile would cost
# minutes on a Windows runner for a file whose location is well known.
$roots = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Packages", "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\wsl") |
  Where-Object { Test-Path $_ }
if ($roots) {
  # No backtick continuations anywhere in this step: a single trailing
  # space after one silently turns it into a syntax error, and this
  # script cannot be parse-checked on a macOS or Linux host.
  $vhdx = Get-ChildItem -Path $roots -Recurse -Depth 3 -Filter 'ext4.vhdx' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  $report += $vhdx |
    Select-Object FullName, @{n='SizeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Length/1GB,2)}} |
    Out-String
}
$report | Tee-Object -FilePath wsl-diag/host-postmortem.txt

set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/status"
# `result` is the CELL's conclusion. The test step fails the producer
# directly; folding L1 remains defensive and keeps the status format
# correct if GitHub reports a healthy job during an `always()` step.
result="$JOB_STATUS"
if [ "$result" = "success" ] && [ "$L1" = "failure" ]; then
  result=failure
  echo "::error title=${PACKAGE} ${JOB} (${ENVIRONMENT}) failed::the L1 suite failed in the WSL2 guest."
fi
# Name WHY no evidence exists, when that is the case.
#
# A guest that dies takes the staging step with it, `wsl-junit` stays
# empty, and `if-no-files-found: ignore` uploads nothing successfully —
# so the rollup could only say "produced no report at all", which reads
# identically to a tier that ran and had no tests. Only the producer
# can tell those apart, so it says which.
#
# A failing TEST needs no detail: the guest stays healthy, staging
# succeeds, and the report the rollup reads is uploaded normally.
detail=""
# First: a refused build status skips provisioning, which must not
# then be reported as a guest that failed to provision.
if [ "$BUILD_STATUS" = "failure" ]; then
  detail="build ${BUILD_KEY} produced on ${BUILD_PRODUCER} has no successful build status; the guest was not provisioned and no test was started"
elif [ "$PROVISION" != "success" ]; then
  detail="the WSL2 guest failed to provision (attempt 1: ${PROVISION_FIRST}, attempt 2: ${PROVISION}); no test could run"
elif [ "$VERIFIED" != "success" ]; then
  detail="build ${BUILD_KEY} produced on ${BUILD_PRODUCER} was refused by the guest's verification (${VERIFIED}); no test was started and nothing was compiled to replace it"
elif [ "$STAGED" != "success" ]; then
  detail="the WSL2 guest became unreachable after the test step (L1: ${L1}, staging: ${STAGED}); its reports could not be collected"
fi
# This cell's stages. The guest cannot write `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, so each
# window it measured crossed the 9p mount as a file; a guest that died
# leaves none, and the stage reports 0 rather than a fabricated
# duration. Reporting only — the cell's identity stays
# {package, environment, gate}.
# Anything that is not a plain count reports 0. This step runs under
# `always()` and is the cell's only evidence: instrumentation must not
# be able to lose it.
number() {
  case "${1:-}" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) echo 0 ;;
    *) echo "$1" ;;
  esac
}
read_seconds() {
  if [ -f "wsl-timing/$1" ]; then
    number "$(tr -cd '0-9' <"wsl-timing/$1")"
  else
    echo 0
  fi
}
extract_ms=0
if [ -f wsl-timing/verdict.json ]; then
  extract_ms="$(jq -r '.timings.extract_ms // 0' wsl-timing/verdict.json 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
fi
timings="$(jq -cn \
  --argjson download "$(number "${DOWNLOAD_SECONDS:-}")" \
  --argjson verify "$(read_seconds verify.seconds)" \
  --argjson extract "$(number "$extract_ms")" \
  --argjson execute "$(read_seconds l1.seconds)" \
  '{download_seconds: $download, verify_seconds: $verify,
    extract_ms: $extract, execute_seconds: $execute}')"
jq -cn \
  --arg package "$PACKAGE" --arg job "$JOB" --arg environment "$ENVIRONMENT" \
  --arg result "$result" --arg detail "$detail" \
  --arg key "${BUILD_KEY:-}" --arg producer "${BUILD_PRODUCER:-}" \
  --arg digest "${BUILD_DIGEST:-}" \
  --argjson timings "$timings" \
  '{package: $package, job: $job, environment: $environment, result: $result}
   + (if $detail == "" then {} else {detail: $detail} end)
   + (if $key == "" then {}
      else {build: {key: $key, producer: $producer, digest: $digest}} end)
   + {timings: $timings}' \
  >"$RUNNER_TEMP/status/status.json"

set -euo pipefail
scope_args=()
if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
  # A manual full run has no diff range. Its plan records the
  # all-zero "no such object" ID as the base, the same identity a
  # branch-creating push carries in `github.event.before`, and the
  # tested head; no receipt is verified against that pair.
  base="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
  head="$PUSH_HEAD"
  scope_args=(--all)
else
  if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "pull_request" ]]; then
    base="$PR_BASE"
    head="$PR_HEAD"
  elif [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "schedule" ]]; then
    # The nightly has no single comparison base: each scheduled
    # environment is planned from the diff since the newest
    # successful nightly that proved IT (or the full gated
    # workspace, with a coded reason), so a WSL2-only history never
    # shortens Windows' scope. The planner derives every diff
    # itself from the anchors, and the plan records the all-zero
    # "no single base" identity. A lookup failure degrades inside
    # `nightly-anchors` to a visible full-scope fallback, never to
    # a narrower plan.
    python3 scripts/ci/reuse_validation.py nightly-anchors > nightly-anchors.json
    # Earlier nightlies' finished hosted cells whose run never
    # reached `publish-observations` (force-cancelled, lost runner,
    # timed out) exist only as `observation-*` artifacts. Record the
    # newest scheduled runs' ones in THIS checkout's notes (no push:
    # this job writes nothing remote) BEFORE planning: the planner
    # reopens an anchored cell that a recovered failure contradicts,
    # and the verifier below vouches for recovered passes like any
    # other observation. A failure here only costs reuse, so it
    # warns and carries on.
    recovery_status=0
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='github-actions[bot]' \
    GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
    GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='github-actions[bot]' \
    GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
      python3 scripts/ci/hosted_observations.py publish \
        --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --recent --no-push \
      || recovery_status=$?
    if (( recovery_status != 0 )); then
      echo "::warning title=CI scope::recovering earlier nightlies' hosted observations ended with exit ${recovery_status}; a cell it could not recover executes"
    fi
    base="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
    head="$PUSH_HEAD"
  else
    base="$PUSH_BASE"
    head="$PUSH_HEAD"
  fi

  if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "schedule" ]]; then
    # The probe lets a hosted passing retry supersede a failure on
    # a cell the anchor would otherwise lend this run.
    scope_args=(--anchors nightly-anchors.json --artifact-repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY")
  elif [[ -z "$base" || "$base" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
    scope_args=(--all)
  else
    # One diff, two lists. `--name-status` is what separates a
    # deletion from a path that is merely absent; `diff_scope.py`
    # turns the stream into `--deleted <path>... -- <changed path>...`
    # so the change inventory carries that identity and the
    # archive-path guard never has to guess. The arguments land in a
    # file rather than a process substitution: `pipefail` sees a
    # failing diff or parse there, and would not see it there.
    diff_arguments="$(mktemp)"
    git diff --name-status -z "$base" "$head" | python3 scripts/ci/diff_scope.py > "$diff_arguments"
    mapfile -d '' scope_args < "$diff_arguments"
    rm -f "$diff_arguments"
  fi
fi

# The event decides which environments are planned
# (`environments.json` `events`); a scope receipt planned for
# another event is refused below for the same reason.
event_args=(--event "$EVENT_NAME")
if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "pull_request" && "${ALL_ENVIRONMENTS:-}" == "true" ]]; then
  event_args+=(--all-environments)
fi
if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "push" && "${PROVEN_BY_PULL_REQUEST:-}" == "true" ]]; then
  event_args+=(--proven-event pull_request)
fi
# Ahead of the file list: after its `--` argparse reads everything,
# options included, as a path. (A nightly's `--anchors` is the whole
# selection input: it carries no file list.)
scope_args=(--plan-out resolved-plan.json --base "$base" --head "$head" "${event_args[@]}" "${scope_args[@]}")

# A scope receipt on refs/notes/ci-local/scope that binds this
# event's exact {base, head, tree} IS the plan: selection never runs
# again for it, with or without validation evidence. Any miss — no
# note, another schema, head, tree, base, or event, or a malformed
# document — calculates scope exactly as before. A manual or nightly
# run and a branch-creating push carry no comparison base and never
# consult the note, and a push whose pull request validation is
# reused plans a narrower set than any receipt holds. A receipt is
# planned for the event's own environments, so a `ci:all-os` pull
# request never takes one: the hook publishes a receipt on every
# push, and taking it silently dropped the label.
local_scope=0
scope_source="CI (no comparison base)"
if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "workflow_dispatch" || "$EVENT_NAME" == "schedule" ]]; then
  scope_source="CI ($EVENT_NAME ignores local scope)"
elif [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "pull_request" && "${ALL_ENVIRONMENTS:-}" == "true" ]]; then
  scope_source="CI (ci:all-os plans every environment)"
elif [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "push" && "${PROVEN_BY_PULL_REQUEST:-}" == "true" ]]; then
  scope_source="CI (reused pull request validation narrows the plan)"
elif [[ -n "$base" && ! "$base" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
  if python3 scripts/ci/local_evidence.py scope-verify \
      --base "$base" --head "$head" --event "$EVENT_NAME" \
      --plan-out resolved-plan.json --scope-out scope.json \
      --reason-out scope-reason.txt; then
    local_scope=1
    scope_source="local (refs/notes/ci-local/scope @ ${head:0:9})"
  else
    reason="$(cat scope-reason.txt 2>/dev/null || true)"
    scope_source="CI fallback (${reason:-scope-verify failed})"
  fi
fi
if (( local_scope )); then
  scope_json="$(cat scope.json)"
else
  # Selection reads `cargo metadata`, so this is the one place the
  # scope job needs Rust: a runner without the pinned toolchain
  # installs it here and nowhere else. A receipt hit never reaches
  # this branch — scope-verify, verify --cells, --apply-to, jq, and
  # the summary need no toolchain (R9: the valid-receipt path pays
  # for no Rust it does not use).
  rustup show
  scope_json="$(python3 scripts/ci/affected_scope.py "${scope_args[@]}")"
fi
evidence_failure=""
if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" != "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
  # Per CELL, across every environment's notes ref at once: a macOS
  # receipt and a prior WSL cross-check receipt both contribute.
  # Each accepted cell has its EXECUTION omitted while staying a
  # cell, so the rollup expects a local-origin result for it rather
  # than reporting MISSING (the PR #76 regression). Every refusal
  # carries a coded reason and is published with the plan.
  #
  # Evidence PROCESSING adds work, never removes it (R8): a verifier
  # that crashes or prints anything but a JSON list, or an overlay
  # that fails, leaves the plan in hand — the receipt's on a hit,
  # this run's calculation on a miss — exactly as it was, reuses no
  # cell, and says so in the summary and a warning annotation. The
  # overlay writes its result beside the plan and replaces it only
  # on success, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a half-written
  # resolved-plan.json for the fan-out.
  verifier_status=0
  python3 scripts/ci/local_evidence.py verify --cells \
    --plan resolved-plan.json \
    --base "$base" \
    --head "$head" \
    --artifact-repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --rejections evidence-rejections.json > accepted-cells.json \
    || verifier_status=$?
  if (( verifier_status != 0 )); then
    evidence_failure="verifier failed (exit ${verifier_status})"
  elif ! jq -e 'type == "array"' accepted-cells.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    evidence_failure="verifier output is not a JSON list"
  elif [[ "$(jq -r 'length' accepted-cells.json)" != "0" ]] \
      || jq -e 'type == "array" and length > 0' evidence-rejections.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # One evidence path for both scope sources: the accepted set is
    # overlaid on the plan already in hand and the projection is
    # re-derived from the result. `--apply-to` performs no
    # selection and reads nothing from the checkout, so a receipt's
    # areas, packages, gates, targets, features, and environment
    # policy reach the fan-out exactly as the hook resolved them.
    # A refusal with nothing accepted takes the same path, so an
    # all-rejected verification still publishes its coded reasons
    # as `evidence_rejections`; only a verification that saw no
    # evidence at all leaves the plan, and the planner, untouched.
    overlay_status=0
    overlaid_json="$(
      python3 scripts/ci/affected_scope.py \
        --apply-to resolved-plan.json \
        --accepted-cells accepted-cells.json \
        --evidence-rejections evidence-rejections.json \
        --plan-out applied-plan.json
    )" || overlay_status=$?
    if (( overlay_status == 0 )); then
      mv applied-plan.json resolved-plan.json
      scope_json="$overlaid_json"
    else
      evidence_failure="overlay failed (exit ${overlay_status})"
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -n "$evidence_failure" ]]; then
    # Nothing downstream may read a partial accepted set.
    printf '[]' > accepted-cells.json
    rm -f applied-plan.json
    echo "::warning title=CI scope::local evidence ${evidence_failure}; the plan runs unmodified and no cell is reused"
  fi
fi
packages="$(jq -c '.packages' <<<"$scope_json")"

# The full scope document is also the rollup's policy source: it
# carries every impacted package's resolved `[package.metadata.ci]`
# policy (gating and `gates = false` alike). Uploaded as an artifact
# so each area's coverage audit sees exactly what this run scheduled.
printf '%s' "$scope_json" > scope.json

# One caller identity per scheduled AREA, each carrying its own
# dispatch rows. Grouping happens in the planner, not here, so the
# shape has test coverage. There is no canary stage: the
# compile check that gates each package's own tests is a cheaper and
# strictly better predictor than a sample of two other packages, and
# it cannot stall the fan-out because it runs inside it.

{
  echo "scheduled_areas=$(jq -c '.scheduled_areas' <<<"$scope_json")"
  # The dispatch rows, one document per area. `jq -c` preserves key
  # order, and it has to: GitHub renders a matrix job's label from
  # the row's values in the order they appear (ruling R1), so a
  # key-sorting serializer anywhere on this path degrades every
  # producer label to `test (macos-latest, L1, pkg, macos-latest)`.
  echo "area_rows=$(jq -c '.area_rows' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "area_slugs=$(jq -c '.area_slugs' <<<"$scope_json")"
  # The areas carrying an accepted policy gap, read from the PLAN
  # (the authority on cell state, receipt-carried or calculated)
  # so each area can decide whether to spend a runner on its gap
  # publisher. A skip hint only: the publisher reselects the cells
  # from the same plan, so a wrong `true` publishes nothing.
  echo "gap_areas=$(jq -c '[.cells[] | select(.state == "accepted-gap") | .area] | unique' resolved-plan.json)"
  echo "packages=$packages"
  echo "package_names=$(jq -c '.packages' <<<"$scope_json")"
  # Derived from the SCHEDULED AREAS, not the impacted list: a change
  # touching only `gates = false` packages impacts packages but
  # schedules none, and an empty area matrix under
  # `has_packages=true` fails the fan-out at strategy evaluation.
  # Reading the list the area matrix expands means the two can never
  # disagree.
  echo "has_packages=$(jq -r '.scheduled_areas | length > 0' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "full_scope=$(jq -r '.full_scope' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "sniff=$(jq -r '.flags.sniff' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "area_drift=$(jq -r '.flags.area_drift' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "job_estimate=$(jq -r '.job_estimate' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "preflight_os=$(jq -c '.preflight_os' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "preflight_reason=$(jq -r '.preflight_reason' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "change_class=$(jq -r '.change_class' <<<"$scope_json")"
  # Scheduling is a projection of the plan's producer owners.
  echo "has_builds=$(jq -r '.build_artifacts | length > 0' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "build_producers=$(jq -c '[.build_owners[].environment]' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "build_owner_runners=$(jq -c '[.build_owners[] | {key: .environment, value: .runner}] | from_entries' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "build_artifacts=$(jq -c '.build_artifacts' <<<"$scope_json")"
  echo "build_runners=$(jq -c '.build_runners' <<<"$scope_json")"
  # Read back from the WRITTEN plan, not from `$head`: every later
  # checkout in this run is this value, and `ci-build` refuses any
  # checkout that is not `plan.head`.
  echo "head=$(jq -r '.head' resolved-plan.json)"
  echo "coverage_environments=$(jq -c '[(.coverage_anchors // [])[].environment]' resolved-plan.json)"
} >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# Evidence provenance, read from the WRITTEN plan (the authority on
# what was reused) rather than from the verifier's transient files,
# so the rows describe exactly what the fan-out will see — on an
# evidence-processing failure that is the unmodified plan, and the
# rows honestly read `none`. The verifier does not report which
# refs it walked; it walks every fetched `refs/notes/ci-local/<env>`
# ref, so those are the environments listed as consulted, and the
# reused cells' environments are the ones that matched. A rejection
# names one candidate note (or one cell of it), not a plan cell, so
# the retained row counts them by code; the full texts ride in the
# plan artifact's `evidence_rejections`.
reuse_row='def cells(f): [.cells[] | select(f)
  | "\(.package)/\(.environment)/\(.gate)"]
  | if length == 0 then "none" else "\(length): \(join(", "))" end;'
reused_passing="$(jq -r "$reuse_row"' cells(.execution == "reuse" and .evidence.outcome == "pass")' resolved-plan.json)"
retained="$(jq -r '(.evidence_rejections // []) as $rejections
  | if ($rejections | length) == 0 then "none"
    else "\($rejections | length) rejection(s): \(
      [$rejections[] | split(":")[0]] | group_by(.) | map("\(.[0]) (\(length))") | join(", "))"
    end' resolved-plan.json)"
if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
  validation_environments="n/a ($EVENT_NAME runs no verifier)"
else
  consulted="$(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:strip=3)' 'refs/notes/ci-local/' \
    | jq -Rrs '[split("\n")[] | select(length > 0 and . != "scope")] | join(", ")')"
  matched="$(jq -r '[.cells[] | select(.execution == "reuse") | .environment] | unique | join(", ")' resolved-plan.json)"
  if [[ -z "$consulted" ]]; then
    validation_environments="none"
  else
    validation_environments="consulted: ${consulted}; matched: ${matched:-none}"
  fi
fi

# One actionable scope summary (D15).
{
  echo "## CI scope"
  echo ""
  echo "| field | value |"
  echo "|---|---|"
  echo "| event | ${EVENT_NAME} |"
  echo "| scope source | ${scope_source} |"
  if [[ -n "$evidence_failure" ]]; then
    echo "| evidence processing | ${evidence_failure}; no cell reused |"
  fi
  echo "| validation environments | ${validation_environments} |"
  echo "| reused passing cells | ${reused_passing} |"
  echo "| cells (execute / reuse / accepted gap) | $(jq -r '[.cells[] | select(.execution == "execute")] | length' resolved-plan.json) / $(jq -r '[.cells[] | select(.execution == "reuse")] | length' resolved-plan.json) / $(jq -r '[.cells[] | select(.state == "accepted-gap")] | length' resolved-plan.json) |"
  echo "| coverage anchors | $(jq -r '(.coverage_anchors // []) | if length == 0 then "n/a" else map("\(.environment): \(.reason)") | join("; ") end' resolved-plan.json) |"
  echo "| cells retained (evidence incomplete or rejected) | ${retained} |"
  echo "| change class | $(jq -r '.change_class' <<<"$scope_json") |"
  echo "| full scope | $(jq -r '.full_scope' <<<"$scope_json") |"
  echo "| full-scope gates | $(jq -rc '.full_scope_gates | join(", ")' <<<"$scope_json") |"
  echo "| reason | $(jq -r '.preflight_reason' <<<"$scope_json") |"
